events.title: Xiongnu Empire Rises
events.description: Modu Chanyu unified tribes across the Mongolian Plateau, establishing the powerful Xiongnu Empire. The Xiongnu became the greatest threat to northern China, forcing the Han Dynasty to build the Great Wall.

events.title: Turkic Khaganate
events.description: Turkic peoples established the Turkic Khaganate on the Mongolian Plateau, controlling Silk Road trade. Turkic culture profoundly influenced Central Asia and Mongolia.

events.title: Uyghur Khaganate
events.description: Uyghur people established the Uyghur Khaganate, becoming the Mongolian Plateau's major power. Uyghurs maintained close relations with Tang Dynasty, helping suppress the An Lushan Rebellion.

events.title: Mongol Tribal Fragmentation
events.description: The Mongolian Plateau fell into tribal fragmentation, with tribes warring among themselves. This period laid the foundation for Genghis Khan's unification.

events.title: Birth of Temüjin (Genghis Khan)
events.description: Temüjin was born into Mongol nobility. His childhood was harsh; after his father's poisoning, the family fell into hardship. These experiences shaped his resilient character.

events.title: Genghis Khan Unifies Mongolia
events.description: Temüjin was proclaimed 'Genghis Khan' at a kurultai, unifying Mongol tribes. This marked the establishment of the Mongol Empire, beginning the Mongol conquest of the world.

events.title: Conquest of Jin Dynasty
events.description: Genghis Khan began conquering the Jin Dynasty (Jurchen rule of northern China). Mongol cavalry was unstoppable, gradually weakening Jin, which finally fell in 1234.

events.title: Western Campaign Against Khwarezm
events.description: Genghis Khan launched western campaign against Khwarezm (present-day Central Asia), avenging caravan massacre. Mongol armies swept across Central Asia, capturing Samarkand and Bukhara, establishing a trans-Eurasian empire.

events.title: Death of Genghis Khan
events.description: Genghis Khan died during the conquest of Western Xia at age 65. He left behind a vast empire spanning Eurasia, becoming one of history's greatest conquerors.

events.title: Ögedei Becomes Great Khan
events.description: Genghis Khan's third son Ögedei was elected Great Khan, continuing Mongol expansion. Ögedei built Karakorum as capital, improving Mongol governance.

events.title: Western Campaign to Europe
events.description: Batu Khan led Mongol armies westward, conquering Russia, Poland, Hungary. Mongol cavalry reached Central Europe's Adriatic coast, shocking the European world.

events.title: Möngke Khan Era
events.description: Möngke Khan reformed Mongol governance, conducting census and improving tax systems. He sent Hulagu west and Kublai south, continuing Mongol expansion.

events.title: Conquest of Baghdad
events.description: Hulagu's army conquered Baghdad, ending the Abbasid Caliphate that had lasted 500 years. This was one of the Mongol Empire's most significant conquests.

events.title: Kublai Khan Becomes Great Khan
events.description: Kublai Khan succeeded as Great Khan. He moved the capital to Dadu (Beijing), adopting Chinese governance, promoting Sinicization. This marked a shift in the Mongol Empire's direction.

events.title: Yuan Dynasty Established
events.description: Kublai Khan changed the state name to 'Great Yuan,' formally establishing the Yuan Dynasty. This was the first time China was entirely ruled by a foreign ethnic group.

events.title: Yuan Conquers Song
events.description: Yuan forces destroyed the Southern Song Dynasty, achieving complete unification of China. Mongols became rulers of the world's most populous region.

events.title: Yuan Falls, Northern Yuan Begins
events.description: Ming Dynasty expelled Yuan forces from China. Mongol royal family retreated to the Mongolian Plateau, establishing Northern Yuan. Mongolian power significantly weakened.

events.title: Altan Khan and Tibetan Buddhism
events.description: Mongol Altan Khan met Tibetan Buddhist leader, conferring the title 'Dalai Lama.' Tibetan Buddhism began spreading across Mongolia, becoming the dominant Mongol religion.

events.title: Qing Conquers Mongolia
events.description: Qing Dynasty gradually conquered Mongol tribes. Outer Mongolia, Inner Mongolia, and Xinjiang Mongolia all submitted to Qing. Mongolia entered over 200 years of Qing rule.

events.title: Outer Mongolia Declares Independence
events.description: After Xinhai Revolution, Outer Mongolia declared independence from Qing rule, establishing the Bogd Khanate with the 8th Jebtsundamba Khutuktu as monarch. However, independence wasn't internationally recognized.

events.title: Tripartite Agreement
events.description: Russia, China, and Mongolia signed the Tripartite Agreement, granting Outer Mongolia autonomy under Chinese suzerainty. Mongolia became semi-independent.

events.title: Chinese Forces Occupy Mongolia
events.description: After the Russian Revolution, Chinese warlord Xu Shuzheng sent troops to occupy Outer Mongolia, canceling its autonomy. Mongolia re-entered Chinese control.

events.title: Mongolian Revolution
events.description: Mongolian revolutionaries, with Soviet Red Army support, liberated Ulaanbaatar, driving out Chinese forces. The Mongolian People's Government was established, though maintaining nominal monarchy.

events.title: Mongolian People's Republic Founded
events.description: After the Bogd Khan's death, Mongolia abolished monarchy and proclaimed the Mongolian People's Republic, becoming the world's second socialist country (after the USSR).

events.title: Choibalsan's Rise
events.description: Khorloogiin Choibalsan gradually controlled Mongolian politics, becoming Mongolia's 'Stalin.' He implemented political purges, eliminating opponents.

events.title: Great Purge
events.description: Under Soviet influence, Mongolia conducted large-scale political purges. Thousands of lamas, nobles, and intellectuals were executed; thousands of temples destroyed. This was Mongolia's darkest period.

events.title: Battle of Khalkhin Gol
events.description: Japanese Kwantung Army and Mongol-Soviet forces clashed at Khalkhin Gol. Soviet-Mongol forces achieved decisive victory, preventing Japanese invasion of Mongolia.

events.title: Independence Referendum
events.description: After WWII, Mongolia held independence referendum with 100% voting for independence. Republic of China recognized Mongolian independence (later repudiated by Taiwan).

events.title: Death of Choibalsan
events.description: Choibalsan died; Yumjaagiin Tsedenbal succeeded, ruling Mongolia for 32 years. Mongolia entered relative stability but remained tightly controlled by USSR.

events.title: Mongolia Joins UN
events.description: Mongolia joined the United Nations, gaining international recognition. However, Mongolia remained closely aligned with the Soviet bloc.

events.title: Sino-Mongol Border Tensions
events.description: Following Sino-Soviet split, Sino-Mongol relations deteriorated. Mongolia deployed large Soviet forces on the Chinese border, becoming a Soviet forward base.

events.title: Sino-Mongol Relations Normalize
events.description: With Soviet reform, Sino-Mongol relations normalized. This laid groundwork for Mongolia's subsequent political and economic transformation.

events.title: Democratic Revolution
events.description: Influenced by Eastern European changes, Mongolia experienced a peaceful democratic revolution. The ruling Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party was forced to abandon one-party rule, beginning political and economic transition.

events.title: New Constitution and Democracy
events.description: Mongolia adopted a new constitution, changing the country's name to 'Mongolia,' abandoning socialism, and establishing parliamentary democracy and market economy. Mongolia successfully achieved peaceful transition.

events.title: First Power Transition
events.description: Opposition Democratic Union won elections, ending Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party's 75-year rule. Mongolia achieved first democratic power transition.

events.title: Mining Economy Boom
events.description: Mongolia discovered massive copper, coal, and gold deposits. Foreign investment poured in; the economy grew rapidly. Mining became Mongolia's pillar industry.

events.title: Oyu Tolgoi Mine Agreement
events.description: Mongolia reached investment agreement with Rio Tinto for Oyu Tolgoi copper-gold mine, one of world's largest. This became Mongolia's most important economic project.

events.title: Air Pollution Crisis
events.description: Ulaanbaatar's air pollution became world's worst, especially severe in winter. Coal heating and ger district emissions caused serious health problems.

events.title: COVID-19 Pandemic Response
events.description: Mongolia closed borders early, successfully controlling COVID-19 spread. However, border closures severely impacted economy dependent on foreign trade.

events.title: Third Neighbor Policy
events.description: Sandwiched between China and Russia, Mongolia actively pursues 'third neighbor' diplomacy, strengthening relations with US, Japan, EU, maintaining diplomatic balance.
